title: Multi-organ proteomic atlas of obesity regression in male mice
projectDescription: Obesity drives systemic metabolic dysfunction, yet how the body adapts and recovers at a system-wide level remains unclear. Here we generate a multi-tissue proteomic atlas of diet-induced obesity and its regression in mice. Using a standardized, semi-automated sample preparation workflow, we quantify 12,936 unique proteins across 15 organs and 4 timepoints. We found proteomic changes to be highly tissue-dependent with a small number of proteins displaying shared changes across multiple tissues. While proteomes of most tissues revert to lean levels after weight loss, white adipose tissue retains strong phagocytic and inflammatory responses, and brain, kidney, bone, thymus, and spleen display delayed obesity-induced alterations. We map the adipose tissue-specific immune regulators using ligand-target inference and show reduced expression of proteasomal subunits in brown adipose tissue, resulting in stalled ubiquitin turnover. Finally, we make all datasets open access and create an interactive Reactome-based webtool to facilitate further community-driven discovery.
sampleProcessingProtocol: General tissue preparation for mass spectrometry-based proteomics (part 1/2) Tissue dissociation and cell lysis were performed using 1.5x volume of 5 % SDS in 50 mM HEPES buffer (pH 8.0) and sonicated for 15-75 seconds depending on volume and tissue, then brought to a boil for 5 mins and centrifuged at 13,000 rpm for 10 mins. Carefully avoiding the fatty layer in affected tissues, we aliquoted 100 ug of protein into a 10x dilution of 50 mM HEPES buffer (pH 8.0) containing 5 mM TCEP and 11 mM CAA for 30 mins in the dark. Protein aggregation capture was done on Kingfisher (Thermo) by incubation of the reduced proteins for 20 mins with magnetic HILIC beads in 70 % (V/V) acetonitrile, washed twice in pure acetonitrile, once in 70 % (V/V) ethanol, and eluted into 140 ul of 50 mM HEPES buffer (pH 8.5). Proteins were enzymatically digested overnight at 37 C using a LysC and trypsin mixture, 1:100 and 1:200 respectively (enzyme:protein). Peptides were acidified to pH 2.0-2.5 using TFA and loaded onto in-house prepared StageTips for desalting, before elution using a 60 % (V/V) acetonitrile and 0.5 % (V/V) acetic acid solution. Finally, acetonitrile was evaporated using a speedvac and peptides were resuspended in 0.5 % (V/V) TFA, ready for mass spectrometry.   Notes and exceptions to the tissue preparation for DIA (part 2/2) Prior to the tissue dissociation and lysis step, bone was first snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen and crushed to a powder using an in-house constructed metal-sandwich and a hammer. Cell lysis and protein aggregation capture steps were skipped for serum. Whole organ was used in bulk for the following: brain, heart, thymus, kidney, pancreas, bone, iBAT. Organ dissections were made for the following: eWAT, iWAT, liver, spleen, duodenum, distal jujenum, quadriceps. For each tissue, all samples were collectively prepared at the same time and analyzed in succession on the same LC column on our mass spectrometers.  Data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry For each tissue, all samples were collectively prepared and analyzed on the same LC column and mass spectrometer system. Approximately 500 ng of purified peptides per sample were loaded onto an LC-MS/MS system, comprising an EASY-nLC 1000 nanoflow liquid chromatograph (Thermo Fisher Scientific) linked to an Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). For reverse-phase chromatography we used a 20-cm analytical column with an inner diameter of 75 μm, packed in-house with ReproSil Pur C18-AQ 1.9 μm resin (Dr Maisch GmbH), and a flow system using ACN/water containing 0.5% acetic acid, at a flow rate of 0.25 μL per minute. We used a gradient from 3% to 8% ACN over 2:51 min:sec, followed by a slow increase to 35% ACN over 35:02 min:sec, escalating to 45% ACN over 6:07 min:sec, and maintaining at 95% ACN for 5 min:sec. During MS1 scans, we monitored the 350 to 1400 m/z range at a resolution of 120,000, with a maximum ion injection time of 45 ms and a normalized automatic gain control target of 300%. MS2 precursor ions were sequentially fragmented by higher-energy collisional dissociation in a 13 m/z sliding window approach with a 1 m/z overlap between windows to cover the 360.5-1000.5 m/z range across 50 scans. MS2 resolution was kept at 30,000 with a maximum ion injection time of 54 ms.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data was quantified tissue by tissue using SpectronautTM v18.1 (Biognosys), in DirectDIA mode and default settings.
